title: POC scoping with Sunridge Health - security pilot
summary: POC scoping for a security-focused pilot. Discussed success criteria (SLA, latency, accuracy), workload sizing and benchmark plan, timeline for a 6-week pilot, and security/compliance requirements: SOC 2/ISO artifacts, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC model, audit logging, and KMS. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send security pack and SOC2/ISO certs, SE to propose benchmark harness, customer to provide sample prompt set and anonymized workload traces.

transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-12-02 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Sunridge Head of Data Science), Evan Miller (Sunridge CISO), Jorge Alvarez (Sunridge Principal Architect)

Summary: quick scoping call to align on security needs and pilot mechanics.

00:00 Laura: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Laura from Redwood — I'll run through agenda, Marcus will join for the technical bits.
00:14 Priya: Thanks, Laura. We want to make sure this pilot addresses both model quality and our security posture, so Evan and Jorge are on to cover the controls.
00:27 Evan: Yup. From security we're mainly focused on SOC 2 evidence, ISO if you have it, SSO/SAML, RBAC and audit logs, and keys — KMS integration. Also data residency for backups.
00:40 Marcus: Totally, we'll cover what we can provide. Quick note: our hosted offering is easiest for quick pilot but we also support Dedicated and Private if you need VPC/on-prem. For the pilot what's your preference?
00:58 Jorge: Ideally hosted but with strict data controls — we need to ensure tenant-level isolation and audit trails. If that becomes a blocker we can look at Dedicated.
01:10 Laura: Good. For success criteria — let's capture it now: accuracy thresholds on NLU tasks, latency p95 under 600ms for 1k concurrent users (or equivalent throughput), and cost targets per 1k tokens. Is that aligned?
01:30 Priya: Yes, but we want to focus on a set of canonical prompts — clinical note summarization and question answering. We'll provide the prompt set. Accuracy we'll measure by Rouge/L and human spot checks.
01:45 Marcus: Sounds good. For benchmarking, we recommend running two variants: a latency-optimized run (lower batch sizes, faster kernels) and a throughput run (larger batching). We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and token/sec.
02:05 Evan: Can we make sure audit logging captures who called the model, which version, and request/response hashes but not full PHI? That's a must.
02:16 Marcus: Yep — we can log metadata and hashed payloads; full transcript storage is configurable. For Hosted we can enable short-lived retention or no storage. For Dedicated/Private, you control retention.
02:33 Priya: About SSO — we use Okta and would like SAML + SCIM for user provisioning. Also role mappings so clinicians vs. devs have different RBAC.
02:46 Laura: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user sync. For RBAC you can define roles in Console and map via SAML assertions. Marcus can walk through the schema.
03:02 Marcus: Quick technical note: when we say KV cache we sometimes transcribe it as "KV cash" in older exports, but it's KV cache — that's important for warm-start behavior and cost. For pilot we'll recommend prefix caching for repeated prompts to reduce tokens.
03:24 Jorge: Regarding keys, we use AWS KMS. Can Redwood integrate with customer-managed keys?
03:31 Marcus: Yes — Dedicated and Private support customer-managed KMS/HSM. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption with BYOK options and we can provide a KMS integration plan during the pilot.
03:46 Evan: We need to see SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001. Also, do you have pen test reports?
03:55 Laura: We'll send SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 cert, and our security pack which includes penetration test summary. I'll follow up after this call.
04:10 Priya: For workload sizing — our initial set is about 10k requests/day with bursts up to 200 RPS for short windows. Average prompt length 120 tokens, responses ~160 tokens.
04:26 Marcus: Based on that ballpark, for acceptable latency we'd recommend starting benchmark on 2x A100-equivalent GPUs with batching set to target 50-100ms kernel runtimes. That should give room for autoscaling. We'll produce estimated token/sec and cost per 1k tokens in the harness.
04:48 Jorge: Do you support quantized variants for cost reduction? We want to understand quality impact.
04:55 Marcus: Yes — we can run INT8/4-bit quantized models; we'll include quality regression checks in benchmarks, and baseline against FP16 runs.
05:10 Evan: On auditing, we need immutable audit logs, retention policy, and export capability into our SIEM. Does Redwood integrate with Splunk/Datadog?
05:22 Laura: We have audit log exports and can push events to customers' S3 or to SIEM via webhook/forwarder — Marcus will confirm connectors.
05:34 Marcus: We have a Splunk forwarding connector and can provide JSON event schema. Audit events include caller, endpoint, model version, timestamps, metrics. We can redact payloads by default.
05:50 Priya: Timeline — what does a typical 6-week pilot look like?
05:56 Laura: Week 0: onboarding and security docs. Week 1-2: benchmark runs and tuning. Week 3-4: integration tests (SSO, RBAC, audit exports). Week 5: evaluation against success criteria. Week 6: decision and pricing discussion. We can compress but this is safe.
06:19 Jorge: For SAML test, we can spin up a test Okta app and provide metadata.
06:25 Marcus: Good — that's usually all we need. For SCIM we require an admin token for provisioning in test.
06:32 Evan: On data residency — backups and logs must be stored in our region (US-East). Is that supported?
06:39 Marcus: For Hosted we provide region pinning where available; Dedicated and Private give full control. We'll note region for logs and backups in the security pack.
06:50 Priya: Success criteria recap — we need: 1) p95 latency <600ms on canonical load, 2) human-rated accuracy > 85% on summarization task, 3) audit logs exporting to Splunk, 4) SAML SSO + SCIM provisioned, 5) SOC2/ISO certs on file.
07:12 Laura: Great. I'll add those as the acceptance matrix. Any blockers on your side?
07:18 Evan: Only that we need to review the pen test summary and see how redwood handles incident response and SLA.
07:26 Laura: We have an incident response addendum and SLA docs — I'll include those.
07:33 Marcus: For benchmarks I'll propose a harness that runs your prompt set across multiple model configs (hosted FP16, hosted INT8, dedicated FP16) and produces p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and a quality delta table.
07:49 Priya: Perfect. For deliverables — can Marcus include a recommended autoscale policy? We want to avoid cold start spikes.
07:57 Marcus: Yes — we'll recommend autoscale with warm pools and a burst policy. We'll also recommend prefix caching to avoid repeated prompt token costs.
08:10 Jorge: Last question: if during pilot we see a regression in quality with quantized model, what's the rollback path?
08:18 Laura: We support model pinning and immediate rollback to last good variant. Also can route traffic by percentage for canary tests.
08:26 Evan: OK sounds good.
08:30 Laura: Recap of next steps — I'll send SOC 2 / ISO certs and security pack; Marcus will send benchmark harness and autoscale recommendations; Priya to share prompt set and workload traces; Evan to provide Okta metadata. We'll schedule technical deep-dive next week.
08:52 Priya: Thanks all.
08:55 Laura: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "KV cash" -> "KV cache"), speaker overlaps, and some filler words removed for readability.
